title: Umar comes in
hookLine: the fierce Umar, angry, reads Ta-Ha at his sister's house and goes to declare his faith (sirah)
tomorrow: To the land of a just king

cards: A man walks through Mecca with a sword at his side and a plan to end the whole thing. Ibn Ishaq says Umar ibn al-Khattab set out that day intending to kill the Prophet, peace be upon him.

On the way a man named Nu'aym stops him and asks where he's going. Hearing the answer, Nu'aym says: you'd do better to look at your own family. Your sister Fatimah and her husband have already followed him.

teach.b: At his sister's door he hears a murmur. Inside, Khabbab ibn al-Aratt is reading to Fatimah and her husband Sa'id from a written page: the opening of surah Ta-Ha.
When Umar knocks, Khabbab hides, and Fatimah slips the page out of sight. Umar storms in, demanding to know what that sound was.
He grabs his brother-in-law, and when his sister steps between them, he strikes her and draws blood. She says it plainly: yes, we are Muslims. Do what you like.
And something in him stops. Ibn Ishaq says that when he saw the blood, he was sorry, and asked for the page. Fatimah wouldn't hand it over until he had washed.

The opening of Ta-Ha says, in paraphrase, that the Qur'an was not sent down to make the Prophet miserable, but as a reminder for the one who fears God, from the one who created the earth and the high heavens.

Umar read it and said, Ibn Ishaq reports: how fine and noble this speech is. Khabbab came out of hiding. Umar asked where the Prophet was, went to the house near Safa where the believers met, and declared his faith there.
Nu'aym turned him around, but the sword and the anger came with him, until his sister stood her ground.
Then he had to wash before he could read.

teach.h: HOW FINE AND NOBLE THIS SPEECH IS.
teach.b: And then a page did what an argument hadn't.

how: Muslims retell the story of Umar's conversion in sirah lessons and sermons, and some teachers point to it as an example of a page of the Qur'an changing a heart.

games.q: you're Fatimah. your brother has burst in, struck your husband, and drawn your blood. he demands to know what you were reading. what do you do?
o: deny it and hide the page.
say plainly: yes, we are Muslims. do what you like.
games.why: Ibn Ishaq says she stood her ground; when Umar saw her blood he was sorry, and asked for the page.

practice: Take a page you've already made up your mind about: a passage from a holy book, a letter from someone you're angry with, an article from the side you don't agree with.
Wash your hands first, or just put your phone face down, then read slowly, one line at a time, as if you'd never seen it. Look for one sentence finer than you expected, and hold it while you sit.

wordCard.voice: Ta-Ha. Umar ibn al-Khattab, on his way to kill the Prophet, reads this surah's opening at his sister's house and goes to declare his faith. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: two letters that open surah 20, which takes its name from them; Umar read its opening at his sister's house.

carryVoice: Your line: the page turned him. His sister's courage came first. Day seven hundred forty-one, done.
